reasons: The Operator window needs a timed wake. With ControlFlow::Wait (:474, :614, :628), a resting pointer produces no events, so the dwell and the 400 ms wheel idle never fire without WaitUntil(next deadline).

Wall-clock time in a quiet scripted run is load-dependent. Steps land one per iteration on a settled frame (:584-591), and startup and presents have taken seconds under load (window.rs:288-290). A gap over 400 ms between scripted notches would split them into two entries, so the '5 notches = commits 1' proof would flake.
A quiet run exits as soon as presented >= frames and steps are empty (:629-633). The run would exit with the wheel transaction still open, giving commits 0, not 1.

The brief line 'a window run feeds GuiFrame::advance (a dwell tip appears without show_tip)' conflicts with STU-SHL-235 rule 5 (:33458; no tip in a headless or agent-driven session). An agent can run only quiet windows (quiet needs frames, :301-302). The Operator window cannot be run without taking the foreground.
conditions: Operator window: feed elapsed wall-clock time to GuiFrame::advance on each loop pass. Use WaitUntil(the frame's next deadline) when one is pending, otherwise Wait. No polling.

Agent mode, set by the host for quiet windows and offscreen runs: dwell tips are suppressed and advance drives only gesture timers. Add a frame test proving that agent mode shows no tip after advance(1000).

Quiet run: the clock does not run while scripted steps remain, because scripted events are instantaneous. After the last step, elapsed time feeds advance. The exit condition also waits until no gesture timer is pending, within the deadline.

Offscreen drive (gui::drive in gui/mod.rs, an owned path) settles pending gesture timers at the end of the script, the same idle rule, so offscreen and quiet captures stay equal for scripts that end in wheel notches.

ACCEPT the substitute proof. A quiet window run wheeling 5 notches over the field gives commits 1 and revision +1, which proves window.rs feeds advance. set_cursor_position is SetCursorPos (winit windows/window.rs:476-489), an OS cursor warp. STU-SHL-104 (:32306) says 'Cursor warping is forbidden', and test 2 asserts 'no OS cursor warp occurred'.

set_cursor_visible without a grab hides the pointer, but the OS pointer still stops at the physical screen edge, so the value stops there too. At release the cursor reappears wherever the hidden pointer went, not at the press point. That is worse for the Operator than a visible cursor.

ColResize is IDC_SIZEWE on Windows, identical to EwResize (util.rs:162-175). STU-SHL-103 requires the ScrubValue cursor to stay distinct from a splitter's. No splitter sets a cursor in this host today (window.rs has no cursor call), so it is distinct for now.
